Team — forwarding Rivermark's quick legal Qs. Pilot timeline is tight (Rivermark wants starting early July). Quick thoughts:

- Output ownership: we typically license output to customers (non-exclusive) and reserve rights to use anonymized telemetry for model ops. Rivermark is asking for assignment/exclusive ownership which is a material change.
- Training/feedback: we offer an opt-out for using customer data to train general models if they buy Dedicated/Private. For Hosted customers we ask for a feedback license for service improvements with telemetry redaction.
- Telemetry: provide token-level cost & latency metrics; we redact PII and have retention controls (30/90/365 day tiers).

Ben — can you draft a brief counterproposal (one-paragraph) and an annotated Order Form note?
Connor — ops: what telemetry retention toggle options do we have for pilots vs production?
Marissa — flag for sales/leadership: if they insist on assignment we likely need approval and a commercial concession.

Thanks — Laura\nLaura Bennett\Head of Legal Operations (sales-facing)\Redwood Inference

From: ben.carter@redwood.com

Hi Anna — great meeting. Quick proposal to move procurement forward: see the short counters below that we can include in the Order Form / Exhibit A. If Rivermark legal prefers redline format we can produce that too.

1) Output ownership: Redwood proposes a non-exclusive, perpetual, worldwide license to Rivermark to use and commercialize outputs produced by Rivermark's use of the Service. Redwood retains ownership of the underlying model, model weights, and service.

2) Training/feedback: For the pilot, Redwood will not use Rivermark prompt/response pairs or telemetry to train or update our general models. For a production rollout, Redwood requests a limited feedback license to use anonymized telemetry for service improvements; customers can opt-out by purchasing a Private deployment or by an explicit opt-out clause in the Order Form.

3) Telemetry/PII: Redwood will provide aggregated latency and cost telemetry; personal data will be redacted as defined in our Data Handling Addendum. Retention options for pilot: 30 days (default) or 90 days on request.

Next steps: if that sounds acceptable I'll ask Legal to prepare a one-page counter and provide a cleaned PDF (attached).

Best,
Ben Carter\Senior Account Executive\Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Rivermark redlines — legal review + options

Looping the three of you for legal/ops/commercial assessment of Rivermark's redlines: see attached from their counsel. Quick risk matrix:

- Assignment of output ownership: high commercial impact and precedent risk. If we assign outputs, we effectively lose productization rights to things that may be used to improve inference features. Recommend we offer an alternative: a broad license to Rivermark with an exclusive clause limited to their product instance (timeboxed) OR a revenue-share arrangement for any productized derivatives.

- Absolute ban on training/usage: acceptable for pilot if timeboxed, but not for hosted general models. Recommend: pilot-only covenant (no training for X months), with permanent opt-out available under Private deployment or an additional fee.

- PII/audit rights: agree to certification language and limited audit rights (quarterly, scoped) — ops can confirm feasibility.

Connor — can you confirm retention toggles (30/90/365) and whether we can provide an audit report instead of live audits? Ben/Marissa — if assignment is non-negotiable, we should flag to leadership for concession thresholds (credits, price uplift, or restrict to Private).

Thanks — Laura

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Anna Li <anna.li@rivermark.com>, contracts@rivermark.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, connor.obrien@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Jun 2025 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rivermark pilot — output/training questions (counterproposal)

Hi Anna / Rivermark team — thanks for the redlines and for being explicit on requirements. We reviewed internally and propose the following compromise to unblock the pilot while preserving both parties' needs:

1) Output ownership: Redwood will grant Rivermark a perpetual, worldwide, exclusive license to outputs generated by Rivermark's deployment for the duration of the pilot (90 days) and a transferable non-exclusive commercial license thereafter. We will not assign underlying model/code. If Rivermark requires broader exclusivity beyond the pilot window, we can discuss a separate commercial arrangement (revenue share / fee).

2) Training/feedback: Redwood will not use any prompt-response pairs, unredacted logs, or identified user data from Rivermark for training general models during the pilot. For production, Redwood requires a limited feedback license for anonymized telemetry for model improvements; Rivermark can opt out permanently by selecting Private deployment or by paying an opt-out fee outlined in the Order Form.

3) Telemetry & PII: Redwood will default to 30-day retention for pilot telemetry and will provide a quarterly audit report covering PII redaction practices. We will agree to limited, scoped audit rights (30 business days notice) rather than live access.

Next steps: Ben will circulate an updated Order Form + Exhibit A with the proposed language and a tracked redline PDF by EOD tomorrow. If that looks acceptable to Rivermark Legal we can route for signature via DocuSign and target the pilot start the week of July 7.

Appreciate the quick collaboration — Laura

Laura Bennett\Head of Legal Operations\Redwood Inference
